title: Kernel Heatmap Profiler + Prefill-Decode Pacing Simulator for CI Golden Ensembles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark harness lacks per-layer kernel selection visibility and a realistic prefill->decode pacing simulator that reflects production batching and KV cache behaviors. This makes it hard to diagnose regressions introduced by kernel routing changes or attention optimizations and to create robust CI perf gates that avoid false positives from synthetic workloads.

Goal: Build two complementary benchmarking enhancements: (1) Kernel Heatmap Profiler — a low-overhead runtime instrumentation that produces per-model, per-layer kernel-selection heatmaps and latency/cost contribution slices for prefill vs decode phases; (2) Prefill-Decode Pacing Simulator (PDPS) — a replayable simulator that injects prefills and decodes using production-derived arrival distributions, KV cache warm/cold traces, and batching rules so we can synthesize realistic end-to-end latencies for candidate changes.

Deliverables: 
- Kernel Heatmap Profiler implementation in the serving runtime with export to our bench dashboard (CSV + JSON + Grafana-friendly metrics).
- PDPS tool that consumes sampled production trace seeds and outputs golden latency distributions and prioritized failure signals.
- Integration into CI: define per-model latency-quantile sentinels (p50/p95/p99) and cost deltas for the golden-ensemble runs; add an initial set of perf gates to the runtime-1.22 pipeline.
- A migration doc for benchmarking owners describing how to add a model into the golden ensemble and how to interpret heatmap artifacts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Heatmap artifacts contain per-layer kernel selection and per-phase token latency breakdown for >95% of internal test models without >5% added p99 latency overhead during profiling runs.
- PDPS reproduces observed production p95 latency within +/-10% for three representative workloads (assistant-chat, search-snippet, summarization-batch).
- CI gate triggers fewer than 2 false positives per quarter on the canary branch after a 2-week calibration window.

Non-goals: Full replacement of the golden-runbook or exhaustive workload fuzzing; PDPS is intended for regression detection and triage, not final SLA-proof acceptance tests.
